english_source_word_order_explanation: Hebrew verb precedes God; OLT recasts as God — He shaped to expose subject-person while prioritizing the owner's approved typography.

footnote_drafts.english: The Hebrew bara is Qal qatal, third-person masculine singular, with its subject Elohim written after the verb. The separate English He makes the inflected subject visible and is not an independent Hebrew word.
The two instances of et mark definite direct objects and do not require independent English lexical equivalents.

[of His Power] is an editorial theological supplement, not a translation of any Hebrew words in Genesis 1:1. Hebrew בְּרֵאשִׁית (bə-rēʾšît) means 'in the beginning' (its syntax is debated). Genesis 49:3 reads וְרֵאשִׁית אֹונִי, 'and the beginning of my strength'; Deuteronomy 21:17 reads רֵאשִׁית אֹנוֹ, 'the beginning of his strength.' In both parallels, strength/vigor is the separate Hebrew noun אֹון, which is ABSENT from Genesis 1:1; the possessive 'His' is also supplied. The association is theological and intertextual, not a lexical meaning of rēʾšît.

source_alignment.commentary: The prefix b is in; the English article the is idiomatic and not an independent Hebrew definite article in b/reshit. Whether Genesis 1:1 is a temporal dependent clause is debated.

Elohim is morphologically masculine plural; here the finite verb is 3ms, a singular governing construction. God is subject following the verb in Hebrew order.
